title: In 27 mouse thalamic nuclei, bulk cortical input share predicted burst firing in task and rest, but layer-5 driver share and first- versus higher-order class did not (IBL, 97 mice)
abstract: Question: does the connectivity of a thalamic nucleus predict how much its neurons fire in low-threshold-spike bursts in awake mice? We used IBL Brain-Wide Map spike times of 9,941 good units in 27 dorsal-thalamic nuclei (194 probes, 173 sessions, 97 mice, 12 labs). A burst starts after at least 100 ms of silence and continues with intervals of 4 ms or less. Before we computed any burst value, we fixed two structural predictors: S, the isocortical share of afferent tracer density in the Knox 2019 model, and D, the layer-5 pyramidal-tract share of corticothalamic input (Sim1-Cre against Ntsr1-Cre Allen experiments). S predicted nucleus burst fraction: Spearman rho 0.74 (permutation p < 0.0001; session bootstrap 95% CI 0.47 to 0.78; mouse bootstrap 0.42 to 0.79). It held in the task epoch (0.74), in passive spontaneous activity (0.69), after firing-rate control (partial rho 0.73), and when any one lab was removed (0.50 to 0.77). D did not predict burst fraction (rho -0.04, CI -0.21 to 0.25). Higher-order nuclei (LP, PO, MD) did not burst more than first-order nuclei (LGd, VPM, VPL, MG): difference -0.70 percentage points (CI -1.95 to +0.55), unlike an earlier monkey result. Neither predictor separates first-order from higher-order nuclei. S mainly orders midline and intralaminar nuclei (low) against sensory and associative relays (high). Limits: the result is a correlation across nucleus averages; within each half of the S range it was positive but not significant. Bulk tracer data mix layer-6 feedback, layer-5 input and axons of passage. The burst criterion uses extracellular spikes only, and most nuclei had burst counts near an interval-shuffle expectation. Code, pre-registered plan, unit-level burst statistics, test tables and figures are included; Allen-derived predictor tables are regenerated by script.

display.caption: Nucleus mean LTS burst fraction (percent of spikes, 95% session-bootstrap CI) against (A) the bulk cortical input share S from the Knox 2019 model, (B) the layer-5 pyramidal-tract share D from Allen Cre-line experiments, and (C) the geometric mean firing rate. 27 dorsal-thalamic nuclei, 9,941 IBL units. Blue: first-order relays; orange: higher-order relays; grey: other nuclei.

(A) Nucleus mean burst fraction in the task epoch against the passive spontaneous epoch, with 95% session-bootstrap CIs; dashed line is equality. Some upper CIs run past the frame. (B) Spearman rho between each predictor and five burst outcomes across nuclei, with 95% session-bootstrap CIs.
Construct check: values of S and D for first-order, higher-order and other dorsal-thalamic nuclei. Neither tracer-derived predictor separates first-order from higher-order relays.
